atoms.text: This guide configures access for FrameForge, a video transcoding service, to the bucket studio-masters in the same account. FrameForge runs under the IAM role FrameForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to that same account. The service reads mezzanine files from the masters/ prefix and writes HLS segments and playlists to the renditions/ prefix. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/masters/*. In the same policy, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/renditions/*, and allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition for masters/. Do not edit the bucket policy, because a same-account request is authorized when the role's identity-based policy allows it. Confirm that no explicit Deny statement in the bucket policy or a permissions boundary covers these actions. Test by submitting a 1080p source file and checking that the .m3u8 and .ts objects appear under renditions/.

This guide configures access for FrameForge, a video transcoding service, to the bucket studio-masters, which is owned by a different account. FrameForge runs under the IAM role FrameForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads mezzanine files from the masters/ prefix and writes HLS segments and playlists to the renditions/ prefix. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FrameForgeTranscodeRole. That statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/masters/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/renditions/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition for masters/. The role must also carry an identity-based policy for the same actions, because a cross-account request needs both sides to allow it. Confirm that no explicit Deny statement in the bucket policy covers these actions. Test by submitting a 1080p source file and checking that the .m3u8 and .ts objects appear under renditions/.

This guide gives ScanLift, an OCR service for scanned documents, access to the bucket records-scans in the same account. ScanLift assumes the IAM role ScanLiftOcrRole in account 111122223333, which also owns the bucket. The service reads multi-page TIFF and PDF files from the incoming/ prefix. It writes extracted text as JSON files to the ocr-text/ prefix, one output object per input document. Create an identity-based policy on the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scans/incoming/*. Add s3:PutObject for arn:aws:s3:::records-scans/ocr-text/* to the same policy, and allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to the incoming/ prefix. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, since the role's own policy is sufficient inside one account. Check that the role's permissions boundary, if one is set, does not exclude these actions. Validate by uploading a scanned invoice and confirming a matching JSON object appears under ocr-text/.

This guide gives ScanLift, an OCR service for scanned documents, access to the bucket records-scans, which is owned by another account. ScanLift assumes the IAM role ScanLiftOcrRole in account 111122223333, while the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads multi-page TIFF and PDF files from the incoming/ prefix. It writes extracted text as JSON files to the ocr-text/ prefix, one output object per input document. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming account 111122223333 as the Principal, and the statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scans/incoming/*. The same statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scans/ocr-text/*, and a second statement allows s3:ListBucket restricted to the incoming/ prefix. The role needs matching permissions in its own identity-based policy, since both accounts must allow the request. Check that no explicit Deny in the bucket policy blocks these actions. Validate by uploading a scanned invoice and confirming a matching JSON object appears under ocr-text/.

This guide grants PixelPress, an image resizing service, access to the bucket catalog-images in the same account. PixelPress runs as the IAM role PixelPressWorkerRole in account 111122223333, which owns the bucket. The service reads original JPEG and PNG uploads from the originals/ prefix. It writes WebP thumbnails at 256, 512, and 1024 pixel widths to the thumbs/ prefix. Add an identity-based policy to the role with s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/originals/*. Include s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/thumbs/* in the same policy, and do not grant s3:DeleteObject, so the originals stay intact. No bucket policy change is required, because the identity-based policy alone authorizes same-account access. Verify that the bucket's Block Public Access settings remain enabled and unaffected. Test with a 12-megapixel upload and check that three thumbnail objects are written.

This guide grants PixelPress, an image resizing service, access to the bucket catalog-images, which is owned by a different account. PixelPress runs as the IAM role PixelPressWorkerRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads original JPEG and PNG uploads from the originals/ prefix. It writes WebP thumbnails at 256, 512, and 1024 pixel widths to the thumbs/ prefix. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement with arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/PixelPressWorkerRole as the Principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/thumbs/*, and it omits s3:DeleteObject so the originals stay intact. The role's identity-based policy must list the same two actions, because cross-account access requires both policies to allow it. Verify that the bucket's Block Public Access settings remain enabled and unaffected. Test with a 12-megapixel upload and check that three thumbnail objects are written.

This guide lets VoiceLedger, an audio transcription service, access the bucket call-recordings in the same account. VoiceLedger uses the IAM role VoiceLedgerAsrRole in account 111122223333, which owns the bucket. The service reads WAV and FLAC recordings from the audio/ prefix. It writes timestamped transcripts in WebVTT format to the transcripts/ prefix. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/audio/*. The policy should also allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/transcripts/*. If the bucket encrypts objects with a customer managed key, add kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey for that key to the same policy. The bucket policy stays as it is, since same-account access follows from the role's policy. Confirm the setup by submitting a 30-minute recording and checking for a .vtt object under transcripts/.

This guide lets VoiceLedger, an audio transcription service, access the bucket call-recordings, which is owned by a different account. VoiceLedger uses the IAM role VoiceLedgerAsrRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads WAV and FLAC recordings from the audio/ prefix. It writes timestamped transcripts in WebVTT format to the transcripts/ prefix. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/VoiceLedgerAsrRole as the Principal and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/audio/*. The statement also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/transcripts/*. If the bucket encrypts objects with a customer managed key, the key policy must also admit the role for kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey. The role needs identity-based permissions for the same actions, since both accounts must allow the request. Confirm the setup by submitting a 30-minute recording and checking for a .vtt object under transcripts/.

This guide configures DocShift, a document conversion service, to read and write the bucket office-docs in the same account. DocShift runs under the IAM role DocShiftConvertRole in account 111122223333, which also owns the bucket. The service reads DOCX and XLSX files from the source/ prefix. It writes PDF/A renditions to the converted/ prefix, using the source object's base name. Create an identity-based policy on the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::office-docs/source/*. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::office-docs/converted/* to the same policy, and allow s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The bucket policy is not modified, because the role's policy is enough for requests inside one account. Check that no service control policy denies s3:PutObject for this role. Validate by converting a 40-page DOCX file and confirming that a PDF of the same base name is created under converted/.

This guide configures DocShift, a document conversion service, to read and write the bucket office-docs, which is owned by a different account. DocShift runs under the IAM role DocShiftConvertRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads DOCX and XLSX files from the source/ prefix. It writes PDF/A renditions to the converted/ prefix, using the source object's base name. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement with account 111122223333 as the Principal. That statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::office-docs/source/*, s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::office-docs/converted/*, and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The role also needs an identity-based policy covering these actions, because a cross-account request must be allowed on both sides. Check that no service control policy denies s3:PutObject for this role. Validate by converting a 40-page DOCX file and confirming that a PDF of the same base name is created under converted/.

This guide gives MarkSure, a video watermarking service, access to the bucket broadcast-clips in the same account. MarkSure assumes the IAM role MarkSureStampRole in account 111122223333, which owns the bucket. The service reads MP4 clips from the clean/ prefix. It writes watermarked MP4 files to the stamped/ prefix and a JSON manifest listing each processed clip to the manifests/ prefix. Attach an identity-based policy to the role allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-clips/clean/*. In that policy, allow s3:PutObject on both arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-clips/stamped/* and arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-clips/manifests/*. Leave the bucket policy alone, since no cross-account grant is involved. Make sure the policy does not allow s3:PutObject on clean/, so the source clips cannot be overwritten. Validate by processing one clip and comparing the manifest entry with the stamped object's size.

This guide gives MarkSure, a video watermarking service, access to the bucket broadcast-clips, which is owned by a different account. MarkSure assumes the IAM role MarkSureStampRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads MP4 clips from the clean/ prefix. It writes watermarked MP4 files to the stamped/ prefix and a JSON manifest listing each processed clip to the manifests/ prefix. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/MarkSureStampRole as the Principal. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-clips/clean/*, and s3:PutObject on both arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-clips/stamped/* and arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-clips/manifests/*. The statement does not allow s3:PutObject on clean/, so the source clips cannot be overwritten. The role must also hold identity-based permissions for these actions, since both accounts must allow the request. Validate by processing one clip and comparing the manifest entry with the stamped object's size.

This guide sets up RedactFlow, a contract redaction service, to access the bucket legal-intake in the same account. RedactFlow runs as the IAM role RedactFlowJobRole in account 111122223333, which owns the bucket. The service reads PDF contracts from the pending/ prefix. It writes redacted PDF copies to the redacted/ prefix, and it writes a CSV log of redaction coordinates to the audit/ prefix. Define an identity-based policy for the role with s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-intake/pending/*. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-intake/redacted/* and arn:aws:s3:::legal-intake/audit/* to the same policy. Do not alter the bucket policy, because the role's identity-based policy grants the access inside one account. Check that bucket versioning is enabled so that overwritten outputs remain recoverable. Validate by redacting a sample contract and confirming that both the redacted PDF and the CSV log exist.

This guide sets up RedactFlow, a contract redaction service, to access the bucket legal-intake, which is owned by a different account. RedactFlow runs as the IAM role RedactFlowJobRole in account 111122223333, and the bucket belongs to account 444455556666. The service reads PDF contracts from the pending/ prefix. It writes redacted PDF copies to the redacted/ prefix, and it writes a CSV log of redaction coordinates to the audit/ prefix. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement with account 111122223333 as the Principal and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-intake/pending/*. The same statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-intake/redacted/* and arn:aws:s3:::legal-intake/audit/*. The role needs an identity-based policy with the same actions, because a cross-account request must be allowed by both accounts. Check that bucket versioning is enabled so that overwritten outputs remain recoverable. Validate by redacting a sample contract and confirming that both the redacted PDF and the CSV log exist.

This guide grants LoudLevel, a podcast loudness normalization service, access to the bucket episode-audio in the same account. LoudLevel uses the IAM role LoudLevelNormRole in account 111122223333, which owns the bucket. The service reads uncompressed WAV episodes from the raw/ prefix. It writes MP3 files normalized to -16 LUFS to the normalized/ prefix. Attach an identity-based policy to the role allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::episode-audio/raw/*. Include s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::episode-audio/normalized/* in the policy, and allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for raw/. The bucket policy remains unchanged, since access within one account can be granted by the role's policy alone. Check that no bucket policy Deny statement uses a condition, such as aws:SourceVpce, that would exclude the role's network path. Validate by processing a 60-minute WAV file and verifying that the output MP3 is written under normalized/.
